items.issue: The statements 'I never regret any decision' and 'I never doubt my judgment' can conflict with evidence-based belief revision and learning from preventable harm.
items.disposition: Keep on hold; retain only the narrower distinction between self-condemnation and responsible review.

items.issue: The clip says the speaker will bear all consequences but gives no example of acknowledging another person's harm, apologizing, repairing damage or changing behavior.
items.disposition: Do not treat 'buying the consequences' as verified accountability or as permission to repeat the same conduct.

items.issue: Attributing every unwanted result only to insufficient capability may preserve a wrong goal, bad judgment or harmful choice.
items.disposition: Require review of the original goal, judgment, impact and alternatives before applying the improve-capability framing.
